title: 2 Bed · 2.0 Bath Single-Story Modern Scandinavian Residence
designer_rationale: The side‑gallery circulation scheme achieves the highest overall score (85.9) and leads in daylight (87.5) while maintaining perfect privacy (100) and excellent space efficiency (98). A linear corridor along the façade provides natural cross‑ventilation and uninterrupted garden views, reinforcing the Modern Scandinavian focus on light, openness, and a strong indoor‑outdoor connection. Circulation remains straightforward, and the privacy gradient from public front zones to rear sleeping areas is clear and acoustic‑friendly. Site-first planning with North frontage, 4.0ft front setback, and 2 bedrooms across 738.3 sq ft.

construction_spec.reason: RCC framed structure recommended for open spatial layout; load-bearing masonry is viable for single-story compact footprint.
assumptions: External perimeter walls configured as 9.0" (229mm) masonry for weatherproofing.
Internal partition walls configured as 4.5" (114mm) space-saving masonry.
Floor-to-floor vertical rise of 10.5' provides 9.5' clear head room after MEP/false ceiling drops.
Reinforced concrete slab assumed at 5.5" thickness with grade M20/M25 concrete.
Quality standard tier: Standard finishes and construction tolerances.

gemini_critique.reasoning: The side‑gallery circulation scheme achieves the highest overall score (85.9) and leads in daylight (87.5) while maintaining perfect privacy (100) and excellent space efficiency (98). A linear corridor along the façade provides natural cross‑ventilation and uninterrupted garden views, reinforcing the Modern Scandinavian focus on light, openness, and a strong indoor‑outdoor connection. Circulation remains straightforward, and the privacy gradient from public front zones to rear sleeping areas is clear and acoustic‑friendly.
strengths: Strong cross‑ventilation and garden view corridor
Clear privacy gradient with acoustic buffer
Fits Scandinavian emphasis on light and nature
weaknesses: Linear corridor can limit interior flexibility for future re‑configuration
Less central gathering hub compared to hub‑type layouts
Potential under‑utilization of interior width beside the side gallery
suggestions: Widen the corridor at the intersection with the living/kitchen zone to create a semi‑central hub
Add a skylight or clerestory above the corridor to boost interior daylight in deeper zones
Integrate built‑in storage or a narrow service closet along the side wall to preserve floor area
